ipBan.title: Address bans
ipBan.help: An address that fails to sign in too often is banned for a while: it gets no answer from the API until the ban ends. Private addresses (192.168.x.x and the like), Home Assistant and an undeclared proxy on your network are never banned. A whitelisted network is never banned. Can still be banned: a computer of your network reaching Meshloom over a global IPv6 address when Meshloom runs in Docker, Home Assistant, macOS or Windows (whitelist your network's IPv6 /64), visitors behind a public reverse proxy not listed in Trusted proxies, and people sharing one public address. A banned administrator unbans from the local network or with meshloom-admin unban.
ipBan.toggle: Ban addresses after repeated failed sign-ins
ipBan.off: Address bans turned off. Running bans no longer apply.
ipBan.invalid: Failed sign-ins: {{minFailures}} to {{maxFailures}}. Window: {{min}} to {{maxWindow}} minutes. Length: {{min}} to {{maxDuration}} minutes.
ipBan.cli: From the host, even while Meshloom runs: meshloom-admin list-bans, meshloom-admin unban ADDRESS, meshloom-admin whitelist add NETWORK.

errors.auth_ip_banned: Too many failed sign-ins from your address: it is blocked for a while. Try again later, or ask an administrator to lift the ban.
errors.auth_ban_whitelist_invalid: Not an IP address or network.
errors.auth_ban_whitelist_exists: This network is already in the whitelist.
errors.auth_ban_whitelist_not_found: This network is not in the whitelist.
